title: Kemi Badenoch tells PM not to raise taxes to fund social care
description: Burnham first proposed a universal system of social care in England in 2009 when he was health secretary under Gordon Brown. He has vowed to spend pol
body: Burnham first proposed a universal system of social care in England in 2009 when he was health secretary under Gordon Brown. He has vowed to spend political capital on the issue as prime minister.However, he is not the first leader in recent years to pledge to address the issue of adult social care.In 2019, in his first speech as prime minister, Boris Johnson said the Conservative Party would "fix the crisis in social care once and for all".Five years later in July 2024, Sir Keir Starmer faced criticism when Labour scrapped plans for an £86,000 cap on the amount anyone in England would need to spend on their personal care over their lifetime.Liberal Democrat leader Sir Ed Davey, who has pushed for social care reform, said on Saturday: "This has to be the start of a real effort to end the social care catastrophe."He added: "I'll fight to ensure family carers aren't forgotten. We need cross-party consensus, and I hope the PM's door is open."Burnham responded to Sir Ed on X, writing: "It most certainly is, Ed. Let's work together to find some common ground."

schema.headline: Kemi Badenoch tells PM not to raise taxes to fund social care

title: Trump paused attacks on Iran to make space for talks, US ambassador says
description: President Donald Trump has paused attacks on Iran for the second night in a row to give diplomacy more time, the US ambassador to the UN said.Speaking
body: President Donald Trump has paused attacks on Iran for the second night in a row to give diplomacy more time, the US ambassador to the UN said.Speaking to Fox News on Sunday, ambassador Mike Waltz said the president was "giving talks some space, he's giving it a little bit of room".An Iranian army spokesperson said on Sunday that Tehran had halted "retaliatory" attacks in the region in response.The pause follows nearly two weeks of daily US strikes and tit-for-tat attacks, effectively unravelling the ceasefire struck in June.Asked whether Trump had decided against escalation for now, Waltz told NBC: "I wouldn't go that far at all. The president is keeping all options on the table."Waltz also rejected reports in the New York Times, external that administration officials had warned expanding hostilities could dangerously drain a diminished stockpile of air defence munitions."The US military... has everything that it needs to conduct this campaign as effectively as it needs to be," he said.As of Sunday evening, Trump had not spoken publicly on the latest developments, but earlier posted computer-generated images on his Truth Social account that depicted US military planes bombing Iranian ships and Kharg island.Meanwhile, Iran and Oman held several rounds of technical talks in Tehran on Friday and Saturday to discuss management of the Strait of Hormuz, according to Iranian foreign ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei. Disputes over control of the strait reignited US-Iran tensions earlier this month and it remains a major block to permanently ending the war.Iran and the US signed a memorandum of understanding in June to halt military operations and reopen the strait, as well as to reach an agreement to end the war over the following 60 days.But after Iranian forces attacked tankers in the Strait of Hormuz on 13 July, the US resumed airstrikes on the country and reinstated its naval blockade on Iranian ports.Iran retaliated with attacks on US military facilities and bases across the Middle East, killing four American soldiers. The US strikes have since killed dozens of people, according to Iran's health ministry.In the UK, new Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said he would meet his US counterpart Pete Hegseth in the coming week to discuss the strait, which is one of the world's key transport routes for oil, liquid natural gas and other essential commodities. "When it comes to securing maritime freedom and free commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz, that's where we are absolutely aligned," Streeting told the BBC.Earlier this week, oil prices hit $100 a barrel for the first time since May, as the renewed fighting stoked fears over global energy supplies.As the war nears its fifth month, it remains largely unpopular in the US, with a new poll from CBS/YouGov suggesting 57% of Americans are frustrated about the conflict and only 19% optimistic.Thousands of people have been killed across the Middle East since the US-Israeli war with Iran began in February, official figures show, with the vast majority coming from Iran and Lebanon.President Trump is set to meet Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the White House on Tuesday.

schema.headline: Trump paused attacks on Iran to make space for talks, US ambassador says

title: Commonwealth Games 2026: Angharad Evans steps out of shadows into spotlight with Scotland's fourth gold
description: Given Evans qualified fastest - and fastest by a distance - any pre-Games ignorance had already evaporated by the time she strode out into this clammy
body: Given Evans qualified fastest - and fastest by a distance - any pre-Games ignorance had already evaporated by the time she strode out into this clammy, claustrophic cauldron of noise on Sunday.The Cambridge-born athlete could have represented England or Wales through her parents but, after choosing to train at the University of Stirling upon her return from studying in the United States, she opted for Scotland.And the noise that greeted her before - and carried her through - her race was rich reward for that decision.As Evans' impressive nails - adorned with Saltires, the T of a well-known lager brand, Nessie, and the words 'Irn Bru' - sliced through the water, the crowd grew louder and louder, culminating in a huge wave of noise when she touched the wall.Afterwards, she confessed to wondering during the race why she didn't feel more stressed but also thanks the Scottish fans for helping her during the tickly bit."It's not the biggest crowd I've competed in front of, but it's the loudest and the most passionate," added Evans, who was sixth in this event at the Paris Olympics. "I felt their energy and love especially in the last five metres when it hurt."I had the choice of England, Wales or Scotland but Scotland felt right, it felt like home. They made me the athlete I am today and I dreamed of getting a gold and having the crowd roar and this is that but 100 times bigger."Alarmingly for her rivals, Evans' main event is still to come. The 200m on Wednesday was considered pre-meet a more likely medal prospect for her.So could she find herself revelling in the Tollcross atmosphere once more?"I don't think you can top how that felt tonight but we'll see how it goes," she said.

schema.headline: Commonwealth Games 2026: Angharad Evans steps out of shadows into spotlight with Scotland's fourth gold

title: Netanyahu accuses NYC's Mamdani of 'fomenting hate' after arrest threat
description: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he planned to attend the UN General Assembly in New York City this autumn, despite the city's mayor, Zo
body: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said he planned to attend the UN General Assembly in New York City this autumn, despite the city's mayor, Zohran Mamdani, making threats to arrest him.Mamdani walked back that threat last week, acknowledging he lacked the legal power to arrest Netanyahu on a warrant issued by the International Criminal Court, the world's top war-crimes court. The Israeli leader told Fox News on Sunday that he was "not concerned" about Mamdani's previous pledge and accused the mayor of "fomenting hate"."He's supposed to be the mayor of all New Yorkers, Jews, Christians, Muslims, everyone, but he's trying to turn one group against the other," Netanyahu said.Netanyahu referenced a pair of stabbings in New York on Thursday, in which a suspect stabbed a Jewish man and an Asian man just blocks apart.The suspect allegedly shouted the phrase "Allahu akbar" while committing the stabbings, according to police. He has been charged with hate crimes relating to each victim.Both men survived the attacks, which drew condemnations from the city's Jewish and Asian American leaders.In the aftermath, Netanyahu said Jewish New Yorkers were "afraid right now."The mayor's office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.Mamdani, a staunch supporter of Palestinian rights, made his opposition to the Israeli military operation in Gaza a central plank of his campaign last year. In an address last week, he called Netanyahu a "war criminal."As part of that platform while campaigning, Mamdani promised to enforce a 2024 arrest warrant for Netanyahu from the International Criminal Court (ICC), which accused the prime minister of committing war crimes in Gaza.Israel has denied charges that it has committed war crimes in Gaza, and Netanyahu called the charges "bogus".The Israeli military entered Gaza after the Hamas-led attack in Israel on 7 October 2023. About 1,200 people were killed and 251 were taken hostage.Over 73,000 people have been killed in Israeli attacks in Gaza since then, including more than 21,000 children, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.Last week, after the New York Times pressed Mamdani on his pledge to arrest Netanyahu, Mamdani said his administration had reviewed the law and found: "We do not have the independent legal authority to enforce this warrant".Mamdani urged the federal government to arrest the prime minister, and said: "Benjamin Netanyahu is not welcome in New York City."

schema.headline: Netanyahu accuses NYC's Mamdani of 'fomenting hate' after arrest threat

title: The Hundred 2026 results: Trent Rockets beat London Spirit
description: The Hundred men's competition, Trent BridgeLondon Spirit 159-9 (100 balls): Brevis 39 (24); Harrison 2-25Trent Rockets 160-6 (98 balls): Duckett 75 (4
body: The Hundred men's competition, Trent BridgeLondon Spirit 159-9 (100 balls): Brevis 39 (24); Harrison 2-25Trent Rockets 160-6 (98 balls): Duckett 75 (47); Milne 2-25Trent Rockets won by four wickets ScorecardCraig Overton won an entertaining contest against twin brother Jamie as Trent Rockets edged a thriller by four wickets against London Spirit in the men's Hundred.The home side's chase of 160 in Nottingham went down to the wire with 10 needed off five balls, but Craig audaciously ramped for six before calmly ticking off the remaining runs with two deliveries to spare.He finished unbeaten on 20 from only six balls as Rockets earned their first win of this year's tournament."He got me out last year so I had to get some payback," Craig told BBC Sport."It's still a bit weird playing against each other. We're getting used to it after a few years."We're both very competitive - we both always want to win - so I think the family will be happy with how we played it." Rockets' chase was set up by Ben Duckett's 75 from 47 balls at the top of the order, an innings which included 12 fours and two sixes and led an impressive recovery after he lost his opening partner Finn Allen for a duck.Duckett fell with 52 runs needed from 26 balls, which looked to have swung momentum Sprit's way, but Sam Billings' 22 off 10 combined with Overton's knock got them over the line.The Hundred men's competition, Emirates Old TraffordManchester Super Giants 187-5 (100 balls): Buttler 90 (50); Rehan 2-43Birmingham Phoenix 100 all out (97 balls): Ferreira 23 (25); Dawson 3-15Manchester Super Giants won by 87 runsScorecard. TableJos Buttler produced a masterful 90 from 50 balls as Manchester Super Giants demolished Birmingham Phoenix by 87 runs to maintain their perfect start to The Hundred.After making his highest T20 score of 131 against India this month, the England wicketkeeper-batter continued his resurgence, striking seven fours and five sixes to lead the home side to 187-5.It was the second highest Hundred total at Old Trafford and one that Phoenix fell well short of as they were bundled out for 100, handing Super Giants their second win in two matches.The women's fixture was washed out and the men's game delayed by 30 minutes but, once the action got under way, fans were treated to a sensational innings from Buttler.Super Giants suffered early setbacks as Tim Seifert and captain Aiden Markram fell cheaply, but Buttler combined power-hitting with deft touches around the ground to bring up his half-century in 31 balls.Buttler's superb innings came to end with three balls remaining, while Tom Moores added an unbeaten 39 from 17 deliveries.

schema.headline: The Hundred 2026 results: Trent Rockets beat London Spirit

title: What we know so far about the Berlin Pride ramming attack
description: Figure caption, Watch: At the scene of Berlin Pride attackOne woman has been killed and at least 29 others injured after a van was driven into a crowd
body: Figure caption, Watch: At the scene of Berlin Pride attackOne woman has been killed and at least 29 others injured after a van was driven into a crowd at a Berlin Pride event on Saturday night, in what officials say was likely an "Islamist terror attack".The suspect, 21-year-old Abdul Ballout, has been shot and killed during a police operation in west Berlin.German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has condemned the incident as a "heinous" attack. Here is what we know so far.  What happened in the Berlin Pride attack?The attack happened at about 22:00 local time (20:00 GMT). A report was made to police in Berlin that a white vehicle had been driven into crowds at a Pride event in the capital. Hundreds of thousands of people had gathered at Tiergarten park, near the iconic Brandenburg Gate, for the annual event, which is known as Christopher Street Day. Some people were also stabbed in the incident, with a blade officials believe could have been a machete.Shortly afterwards, the Pride event was cancelled. A performance was abruptly brought to a end, with organisers taking to the stage and advising the crowd to start walking towards the exits. As the message was being given to the crowd, the word "evacuation" was projected onto a large screen on the stage. Unverified video posted to social media showed large crowds of people leaving the scene as emergency vehicles raced to the scene. At about 01:00 local time, police confirmed that one woman had been killed and many more had suffered injuries.A short time later, police confirmed they had found the vehicle believed to have been used in the attack, saying it had crashed into a tree. The vehicle is believed to have been rented.Image source, ReutersImage caption, Investigators at the scene in Tiergarten park on SundayAt about 03:30, police said on X they had identified a suspect with Islamist links.The search area was widened to the entire city and involved thousands of police, including officers from surrounding German states.On Sunday, police officers stood guard outside an apartment block in Berlin's Tiergarten district, which is said to be the suspect's home. Police say he was later shot and killed at an allotment complex in Spandau, a borough in the west of the capital, after he rushed at officers with a knife.Who is the suspect in the Berlin Pride attack?The suspect has been named by police as 21-year-old Abdul Ballout, a German citizen of Lebanese background.He was known to police and had been radicalised, officials said.A statement released by the Berlin public prosecutor's office revealed further details about Ballout's criminal history.In May 2025, prosecutors said he travelled via Turkey to Lebanon, with the intention of joining the Islamic State group (IS) in Syria. While in Lebanon he allegedly made contact with several individuals he believed were members of IS.He was arrested in Lebanon in July 2025 and sentenced to three months in prison for incitement to religious and sectarian conflict.Then in November 2025 he returned to Germany where he was arrested at Berlin Brandenburg Airport and held in pre-trial detention.In May this year, he was sentenced to one year and 10 months in prison for "preparing a serious act of violence endangering the state". The decision was deferred for six months and he was placed under the supervision of a parole officer.He was previously convicted of assault and robbery in 2022, and of robbing a victim of headphones in 2020.Image source, Polizei BerlinWhere did the attack happen?The attack took place in the popular Tiergarten park, near the Brandenberg Gate. A large number of people and floats took part in the Christopher Street Day event, which passed through the city, before moving through Tiergarten park, past the Victory Column monument, and towards the Brandenberg Gate. Berlin Police have said people were hit on Ahornsteig, which is a long path stretching across the park, largely in a forested area. European leaders have been swift to condemn the attack.European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen expressed her sympathy to the victims, saying the Pride event stands for "freedom, dignity, and equality - the fundamental values of the EU"."Every person should be able to live, love, and stand up for their rights without fear," she wrote on social media.Rob Jetten, prime minister of the Netherlands, said the Dutch stand "shoulder to shoulder with our German neighbours", while Italy's prime minister Georgia Meloni expressed "solidarity and sincere sympathy".The UK's defence secretary Wes Streeting called the incident "an absolutely horrific disaster", adding his thoughts and prayers are with the German people.Did you attend Berlin Pride? If it is safe to do so, get in touch.Get in touch hereWhatsApp: +44 7756 165803Email: yourvoice@bbc.co.ukPlease read our terms & conditions and privacy policy

schema.headline: What we know so far about the Berlin Pride ramming attack

title: Prince of Wales boat tragedy: Man's entire family never came back
description: My entire family went on a boat trip that they never returned fromImage caption, Peter Watts was just 14-years-old when he lost his mother, father, br
body: My entire family went on a boat trip that they never returned fromImage caption, Peter Watts was just 14-years-old when he lost his mother, father, brother and sister in the boating disasterByGeorge HerdBBC Wales"It's something you don't get over - you learn to live with it."Sixty years ago, Peter Watts' entire family was killed in a boating tragedy that shocked the nation.His nine-year-old sister Angela, 10-year-old brother David, mother Doreen and father Frederick George, along with 11 others, died when the Prince of Wales pleasure boat sank on the Mawddach Estuary in Gwynedd on 22 July, 1966.Now, a memorial recalling the names of the 15 people who lost their lives has been unveiled.It was another chance for Peter to travel from the village he grew up in, near Milton Keynes, to the picturesque estuary where the catastrophe unfolded.Image source, Mirrorpix via Getty ImagesImage caption, Divers search for remaining survivors on the Mawddach Estuary back in July 1966 after the Prince of Wales pleasure boat sank"We'd been on holidays in previous years and I'd been on this boat trip [before] and I didn't want to go again," Peter recalled.Peter was 14 at the time, old enough to be allowed to spend the day on his own in the seaside town of Barmouth, where his family were staying in a boarding house.The rest of his family joined the queue to board the Prince of Wales for the eight mile (13km) trip down the estuary to the George III Hotel at Penmaenpool.Image source, Peter WattsImage caption, Peter's parents Doreen and Frederick George, seen here on their wedding day, died in the tragedyBut the tide pushed the ferry boat into the Penmaenpool toll bridge across the estuary, flinging the 42 passengers into the water as the vessel was wrecked on the bridge.Local people, including the hotel owner and staff and the toll bridge keeper, ran to the aid of those in the water, managing to pull 27 to safety.But along with Peter's brother and sister, two other children were among the 15 who could not be saved.Image source, Mirrorpix via Getty ImagesImage caption, The tragedy led to changes in the law on the number of passengers boats such as the Prince of Wales could carry"This happened in the morning, at about 11 in the morning, and I was just waiting hours and hours for them to come back - and they didn't come back," said Peter."I went down to the harbour and I heard two people talking about a boat that had sunk. I asked them what was going on, and they said what it was, and I said 'My family is on it' - and they said 'Go to the police station'."I sat in there for what seemed ever and a day, and they took the details."The guest house owners came to take him back, while his aunt and uncle drove up to be with him."The next morning we went to Dolgellau to the hospital, where they had found three of them - my mother was still missing," he said."My father could swim, but my uncle who identified him said he had had a nasty blow on his head."It would be another three days before his mother's body was found.Image source, Peter WattsImage caption, This picture of Peter's brother and sister, David, 10, and Angela, nine, was taken only a few weeks before the disasterAn official inquiry found the boat was carrying six more passengers than the maximum 36 permitted under its certification.There should also have been two crew members - one on the engine and one on the rudder.But there was only skipper Edward Llewelyn, 73 at the time, who was found to have acted negligently by a Board of Trade inquiry.The boat was also short of lifebelts and buoyancy apparatus was stowed away.Llewelyn was ordered to pay £100 towards the inquiry costs, but no prosecutions were ever brought.However, the inquiry did lead to changes in the law governing insurance and the number of passengers boats could carry.Image caption, A new memorial to the tragedy names each of the victims, including Peter's familyThe events have left a deep mark on Peter, and the urge to return to Barmouth and the estuary as often as he could."If I've ever been anywhere near Wales, even when I've been going to Holyhead, when we went to Ireland, I'd come round this way," he said."Just to spend a few minutes."Returning this time on the 60th anniversary of the tragedy, it was marked with a special memorial and the plaque to remember those who died, unveiled by Dolgellau Town Council."Those 15 people - I didn't want them to be forgotten. Having their names there - that's what I wanted," said Peter.

schema.headline: Prince of Wales boat tragedy: Man's entire family never came back

title: World Matchplay darts 2026 results: Luke Littler defends title and smashes Phil Taylor's average record
description: Luke Littler defended his World Matchplay title in sensational style - and smashed Phil Taylor's tournament and final average records in the process.T
body: Luke Littler defended his World Matchplay title in sensational style - and smashed Phil Taylor's tournament and final average records in the process.The 19-year-old beat seventh seed Gerwyn Price 18-9 in Blackpool to become just the fourth person to win back-to-back Matchplay titles.World number one Littler finished the week with an average of 111.04, beating Taylor's record of 106.31 in 2010. He averaged 111.53 in the final, setting a new record as he bettered Taylor's 111.23 against Adrian Lewis in 2013.Littler claimed £225,000 in prize money for winning the event and now has £3,143,500 over the PDC's two-year order of merit. That is £2.13m more than Luke Humphries in second spot."It's been a crazy week, one of the best weeks of my life with the darts I've played," Littler told Sky Sports."It's been tough. The stats may look like it's easy, but when you're on this stage with how hot it is, it's not easy."Price averaged 104.97 in the final and has enjoyed a successful week, climbing to fourth in the order of merit and reclaiming the Welsh number one spot from Jonny Clayton.Littler went into the final as the overwhelming favourite and a stunning 167 finish in the fourth leg secured an early break to help him claim the first mini-session 4-1.That form continued as he led 8-2 and was averaging 114.74, with Taylor's record of 114.99 in any Matchplay game in sight.His level dropped slightly in the next two sessions, but he still claimed both 3-2 to push ever closer to the finish line.He moved to within two legs with another brilliant 148 checkout - his sixth ton-plus finish in the final - before a break and hold saw him claim his fourth ranking title of the calendar year.The back-to-back world champion also hit 12 180s in the final to set a new tournament record of 66, surpassing the total he set last year.The run is also continuing his sublime form in longer-format matches - this win extending the streak to 29 successive wins in games with 20 or more legs.His last defeat over a match of that duration was when he burst on to the scene in the 2024 World Championship and lost to Luke Humphries in the final."Luke is one in a million, I threw everything at him," Price told Sky Sports."He's fantastic for the sport. I wish he wasn't as good as he is - I would have won a couple more tournaments."I hope there's no-one else like him coming through because he's ridiculous!"Speaking after the final, Little reiterated his intention now was to try to claim a clean sweep of the PDC ranking titles in the calendar year - a feat never achieved before.The Players Championship Finals in November are a sticking point.It would mean needing to play in, and probably win, some Pro Tour events, and Littler has skipped the first 24 and has already pulled out of the two in Hildesheim this week.That leaves just eight left for him to feature in Minehead. A total of 64 players qualify for that event and the final player currently has £22,750 in prize money.A win is worth £15,000 and a runner-up spot £10,000, so Littler has some work to do."I don't think my dad's too happy because we were going to go to Spain and I think we've got to go to Leicester now and play some Pro Tours, but it is what it is," Littler added on Sky Sports."I've been checking the Pro Tour rankings and whoever is in 64th just keeps going up and up and up. I know there are four in Leicester that I've got to go to now and we'll see what happens."If I don't qualify then I'm going to get grilled and if I do, I'll get grilled anyway. Who knows what's going to happen?"Former BDO world champion Mark Webster said he "half expects" the teenager to achieve the clean sweep."Who is going to stop Luke Littler?" he added."You could argue the first round of the Grand Prix because of the short format [best of three sets], but Gian van Veen threw everything at him last year and he had all the answers."At the minute his game just holds up in any format and scenario. He wants to break records. You definitely wouldn't rule it out."

schema.headline: World Matchplay darts 2026 results: Luke Littler defends title and smashes Phil Taylor's average record

title: Israeli settlers set fire to mosques, cars and farm land in West Bank, Palestinians say
description: Israeli settlers have set fire to two mosques, as well as cars and agricultural land in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials say, as tensions
body: Israeli settlers have set fire to two mosques, as well as cars and agricultural land in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials say, as tensions in the territory continue to flare. The latest attacks come two days after a clash between settlers and Palestinians near the village of Tal, which left four Palestinians and two Israelis dead.Both sides accused the other of provoking the violence. The confrontation has further inflamed the situation in the West Bank, which has seen ever growing violence by extremist settlers against Palestinians, encouraged by far-right elements in the current Israeli government.Palestinian reports say that two villages in the occupied West Bank came under attack from settlers overnight, with cars vandalised, property stolen and hate graffiti spray painted on walls.The mayor of Qusra said that settlers set fire to a mosque that was under construction.Abdul Azim Wadi said that settlers spray painted graffiti that included the word "revenge" on the walls of the mosque.The Israeli military has said that troops were sent to Qusra and that police would investigate and collect evidence.Palestinian officials say that in a separate incident, settlers set fire to another mosque in the village of Kour and sprayed slogans on its walls.Since the deadly clash on Friday in Tal, Palestinians say that there have been multiple settler attacks on villages across the West Bank.The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) has carried out raids and arrested more than 130 individuals over the weekend in what it has called a "counter-terrorism" operation.The Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu responded to the incident in Tal by vowing to take "powerful action".That includes the possible demolition of the homes of two of the Palestinians who were allegedly involved.Kaied Ahmad Turabi, from Miami, was visiting his parents and sister in the village when the attack happened. He was filmed fighting with settlers on a neighbour's porch.He was just out of hospital when he spoke to the BBC. He had a large black eye, several cuts and bruises, and a wound on his head that he said had needed 12 stitches."I worked all my life with Jewish people, but these people... they all had covered faces, all of them had a lot of stuff – sticks, and things in their pockets. They came ready," he said.Hours later, we were with residents watching the back entrance to the village when settlers were spotted on its outskirts again.We watched dozens of young men stream up the road, answering a call to barricade and defend the village.Israeli soldiers stood guard to separate the groups, as the settlers slowly melted away.For the Palestinians, it was a different method of crowd control - tear gas fired repeatedly to push them back down the road.Some young men ran through clouds of gas to try and bury the cannisters with soil, or kick them away to chants of "Palestine, Palestine", as the soldiers steadily advanced.Israel's military said on Sunday it was working to prevent "incidents of nationalist crime" - its term for attacks by extremist Israeli settlers there.But while Israeli leaders publicly condemn extremist violence, they have overseen a rapid growth in the wildcat settlement outposts that human rights groups say are fuelling attacks on Palestinians.Israel's prime minister said he would speed up the establishment and legalisation of farm outposts in the West Bank, in response to the killing of Israelis in Tal on Friday.New Israeli outposts have already appeared in the area since then - one near Sarra is visible from the main road.There has been a sharp increase in settler attacks in the West Bank in recent months.It has drawn international condemnation, but shown little or no sign of being reversed.The situation had already deteriorated before the Hamas-led attacks on Israel on October 7, 2023.But since the subsequent war waged by Israel against Hamas in Gaza erupted, settler violence in the West Bank has escalated.The UN says 1,114 Palestinians have been killed in the West Bank, the vast majority by the IDF. It says at least 35 of the deaths have involved attacks by settlers.It says 41 Israelis, including civilians and security personnel, have been killed in Palestinian attacks or during Israeli military operations in the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war.Israel has built hundreds of settlements housing 700,000 Jews since it occupied the West Bank and East Jerusalem - land Palestinians want, along with Gaza, for a hoped-for future state - during the 1967 Middle East war. An estimated 3.3 million Palestinians live alongside them. The settlements are illegal under international law.

schema.headline: Israeli settlers set fire to mosques, cars and farm land in West Bank, Palestinians say

title: Losing my leg elevated my life, says world surfing champion
description: Image source, BBC | Cwmni Da | Phil BoydImage caption, "Anything is possible if you have any kind of disability," says Llywelyn WilliamsByNicholas Bou
body: Image source, BBC | Cwmni Da | Phil BoydImage caption, "Anything is possible if you have any kind of disability," says Llywelyn WilliamsByNicholas BourneBBC WalesFour-time world champion adaptive surfer Llywelyn Williams says losing his leg as a teenager elevated his life.Surfing played a pivotal role in his recovery and in the years since losing a leg after being hit by a car in 2011.It had been a passion of the then 16-year-old prior to the accident - and it was not going to stop him despite being severely injured while out skateboarding.In fact, he recalled coming around from a coma in hospital amid a dream that a surfboard came between him and a bright light "like you see in the movies"."It wasn't my time," said Williams, from Abersoch, Gwynedd.A friend asked him what he wanted to do while he lay in his hospital bed; he wanted to get back in the water - and go surfing in Australia."The rehab was to drive myself to get back into the ocean," said Williams, known as Sponge by friends. "As soon as I got back in the ocean, I felt like I was born again."When the board and you connect perfect on the wave, it just feels like you're flying."Image source, BBC | Ryan DeinImage caption, Llywelyn Williams (third right) pictured after competing at the 2026 Bright Sky Australian Pro Adaptive Surfing ChampionshipHis mother, Eirian Parry, described the "beautiful moment" his friends carried him into the sea as he continued his recovery following the amputation.But she still recalled with visible emotion the time she and Williams' father faced up to a "nightmare" - when doctors asked them to sign a consent form to amputate their son's right leg.David Williams told BBC documentary Our Lives: Beyond the Waves it was the hardest decision of his life "but it was the only way to save" his son's life."To think he was nearly dead on the side of the road when the accident happened... to being the world champion," he said."Once he got his first wave back, there was no stopping him."His father can also remember tough times early into his son's recovery, one in which he told him he had to be strong while at a low point, and then took himself off and cried in the room next to his son."The way my parents have brought me up is you've just got to get on with it so, yeah, I had one leg and that was it," said Williams.Image source, BBC | Samuel SmithImage caption, He won the 2026 Bright Sky Australian Pro Adaptive Surfing Championship as the kneeling championHe works as a digger driver in the family construction business when not surfing."I've learned how to do everything with one leg, except to be able to use a wheelbarrow," said Williams with a wry smile."When I turned 18 I wheelchaired my way into the kitchen and said we're heading off to Australia."We did a year out there travelling around the coast surfing, living in a camper van."To be able to go back there now every year for a competition is just brilliant."In March, he won the 2026 Bright Sky Australian Pro Adaptive Surfing Championship as the kneeling champion and proudly held the Welsh flag aloft on the beach at Byron Bay, New South Wales.And he was third in the North Shore Prosthetics Hawaiian Surfing Championships in May.He self funds participation in surfing competitions and has been thankful for his supporters close to home.Williams has also been lobbying with others for his sport to be included in a future Paralympics Games."Surfing has been a huge part of my recovery and the adaptive surfing community has helped me so much," he said."Disability for me has elevated my life - anything is possible if you have any kind of disability."Our Lives: Beyond the WavesAfter losing his leg as a teenager, surfer Llywelyn Williams became a four-times para surfing world champion. Now he’s on top of the adaptive surfing world, the challenge is to stay there. Watch now on iPlayer or BBC One Wales on Monday 20 July at 19:00 BST

schema.headline: Losing my leg elevated my life, says world surfing champion

title: Hungarian Grand Prix: Lando Norris and McLaren almost perfect as Ferrari flounder
description: Lando Norris ended the first half of the Formula 1 season with a victory in the Hungarian Grand Prix that he described as "one of my best performances
body: Lando Norris ended the first half of the Formula 1 season with a victory in the Hungarian Grand Prix that he described as "one of my best performances".It was a drive that had been a long time coming, after a difficult start to the season for the reigning world champion and his McLaren team.But when McLaren finally gave him a car of the performance level he had become used to in the past season and a half, he more than made the most of it.While Ferrari, the pre-race favourites, floundered and made, in the words of their team boss Frederic Vasseur "too many mistakes", Norris and McLaren were almost perfect.Even in the context of Kimi Antonelli's stellar start to the season for Mercedes, this was one of the most impressive and convincing victories of the season.Norris' one mistake was on the first lap. He converted his pole position into a lead at the first corner, only to misjudge the grip available at Turn Two, slide wide, and gift his position to team-mate Oscar Piastri.It looked to have been a potentially fatal error to his victory hopes on a track where overtaking is all but impossible between evenly matched cars on similar strategies, but Norris stayed calm.Seeing he could easily keep pace with Piastri despite being in the dirty air, he said he always believed the win was on."It wasn't my finest Turn Two," Norris said, "but after that, seeing what my pace was like and I was just better in every sense, in terms of degradation and pace, I was convinced I could still win the race."Trapped, Norris begged for a different strategy to give himself a chance of victory, and eventually circumstances presented it to him.Around half-distance. McLaren pitted Piastri to cover off Lewis Hamilton's Ferrari, which had just stopped for fresh tyres. That gave Norris clean air and he set a blistering pace.Piastri might still have held the lead, but for a collision with Carlos Sainz as he lapped his Williams. The Australian was angry after Norris came out ahead from his stop a few laps later - but at the Spaniard, not McLaren."The fact I could keep up with Oscar on this kind of track, where it's impossible to follow and impossible to overtake, I was within 0.8 seconds or something for, I don't know, almost 40 laps, the fact I could do this is what gave me confidence that I'd win the race no matter what, whether he boxed early or late or whatever," Norris said."The pace advantage I had was huge today. But I don't know why. The cars are identical, and I've just been feeling very strong lately."I've worked on many areas from last year. I feel much more confident lately with how to extract performance, and I've worked a lot with my engineers to understand this car because it's certainly not an easy car to understand and figure out how to drive on the limit consistently."So, why? Just hard work. Hard work from my engineers and from myself to improve me as a driver and improve my driving. That is the answer."Norris believes he is driving better this season than he did in the first half of his championship year in 2025.Last year, he was struggling for feeling from the McLaren.Like all his rivals, he does not like this new generation of cars as much as the last - especially their engines and the need for so much energy management, and the way they have compromised the driving experience.But he has gelled with them, while Piastri - so strong in the first half of last season - is struggling.Team principal Andrea Stella says this is a continuation of the trajectory Norris has been on since a lot of self-assessment led to his strong second half of last year, and eventually the title."Lando is much more confident. He's much more aware of his tools that he has in his driving, how to deploy these tools. And I think he's also, let me say, more in control of his emotions," Stella said."Because today, when he was behind Oscar, he said a couple of times that he had pace in hand, but he didn't get overly frustrated. And the fact that he wasn't overly frustrated, I think, then allowed him to use the pace at the right time and lead him to the victory. We've seen a great trajectory of development for Lando."This performance came after a major upgrade to the McLaren car, and there is another to come at the next race, the Dutch Grand Prix after F1's four-week summer break.Norris' win moves him up to 98 points behind Antonelli, but he cautioned against expectations of a charge up to the top of the championship of the kind Max Verstappen and Red Bull mounted against him and McLaren last year."I'm just happy with today," Norris said. "It doesn't mean if I'm quick here, we're going to be quick everywhere."One thing I've learned for sure is just to have no expectations of the future and just to work in the present. I think that's the way we've been doing everything as a team."That's why we're back on top today: just working hard on ourselves as individuals and also as a team."Of course, I'm optimistic for the future and I think we can win more races, but we have good competition and there are still plenty of races I'm not confident in because the car is not to the standard that it needs to be in certain areas."During the race, it appeared as if Piastri's anger over the radio might have been partly directed at the off-set strategy that led to Norris passing him for the lead.In fact, he was instead furious with Sainz."The timing of my stop was fine," he said. "We wanted to cover off Hamilton, which was perfectly normal. Without getting crashed into, I would have been ahead of Lando still."In the moment, I was incredibly annoyed. In fact, annoyed is not the word I would use, but there was a multitude that I would, with Carlos. And, yeah, then obviously, when Lando came out ahead, I knew I had no pace to go and attack him."I knew my chances of winning the race were done from there."Discussing the collision with Sainz, Piastri added: "I don't really care if he didn't see me. The fact that he didn't and no-one told him, or there was a lack of complete awareness, is unacceptable."He's quite critical of others, and others have given him some stick before for being frustrating on track."He was not at all mollified by a problem with the GPS system that shows teams where all the cars are on track. Sainz said he had "no idea I was trying to get lapped", he "didn't expect" Piastri to be there, and it was "impossible to avoid it".For Piastri, it was academic in the end, a gearbox failure sending him into retirement and denying McLaren a one-two.As for Ferrari, they appeared to have the fastest car in Hungary, but underperformed in qualifying. Then Hamilton, after qualifying second, was dropped  to fifth on the grid with a penalty for impeding Piastri.Norris will have been worried about Charles Leclerc starting alongside him on the front row. But instead of challenging Norris, Leclerc lost out to Piastri, Verstappen and Hamilton.The seven-time champion got ahead of Verstappen in the first pit stops - only to be overtaken again the next time around, the Dutchman making a brilliant move at Turn One that caught Hamilton napping.A penalty for pit-lane speeding cost Hamilton a further five seconds, and left him behind Leclerc at the end, the Ferraris finishing fourth and fifth.Hamilton, who remains second in the championship, 50 points behind Antonelli, said "you can't make these kind of mistakes if you want to challenge for a title".Vasseur said: "It's difficult to clearly understand the pace, because I think the clean air is key, but first it's not a good Sunday, because when you are one-two on Friday, you expect much more."And on the top we made too many mistakes today, starting with the penalty and the fact that Max overtook us, that each time that we were doing a pit stop, we were losing a position for 0.2 or 0.3 seconds."And then we spent our lives behind the guys, everything went wrong, but for sure we have to do a much better job on Sunday."Norris was followed across the line by Verstappen and Antonelli, both of whom drove fine races themselves, the three podium finishers fully deserving their results.Antonelli's team-mate George Russell, meanwhile, had another day to forget. A problem with his engine at the start, for which the team took the blame, dropped him to the back at the start, and he recovered well to seventh, but still lost points to the Italian, who he now trails by 59 points."I'm sort of past the point of disappointment now, because it's just, if I'm continuing to be disappointed with everything that goes on, I'll just be disappointed every day of the week," Russell said."Obviously, another technical issue that completely ruined the race, but I can tell you some positives. The pace was very strong. "So, I'll take positives there, but yeah, it's just unbelievable, the list of things that's happened this season."Oscar had his thing today as well. It's not like we're the only one, but it does feel like it is happening substantially more to me than others, and hopefully it swings around."I don't wish any bad luck on anyone, but I've never had a season like this in my whole career, let alone my F1 career."Antonelli, then, goes off on holiday in total control of the championship. But he knows to take nothing for granted, as this time last year the same looked to be the case for Piastri."I think Lando still had the upper hand this weekend, even on us," Antonelli said."On pure pace, I don't think I would have been able to challenge him, especially with how difficult it was to follow as well, with a lot of tyre overheating."I did not expect to find myself in this position. But the car has been extremely good, the team has done an incredible job and, on my side, I try to maximise every opportunity I have."Of course, there's still lots of work to do, lots to learn, but it was a good first half of the season. Now I'm looking forward to the second half and we're just going to keep pushing."

title: Ryan Gosling to join Marvel Cinematic Universe as Ghost Rider
description: Ryan Gosling will join the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) as the titular character in a new Ghost Rider film, the media franchise has announced.Speak
body: Ryan Gosling will join the Marvel Cinematic Universe (MCU) as the titular character in a new Ghost Rider film, the media franchise has announced.Speaking during the surprise announcement at San Diego Comic-Con on Saturday, Gosling said it is a character he has "wanted to play for a very long time".The film is due to be released in 2028, and will be the third about the motorcycle-riding anti-hero. It will follow the 2007 film of the same name starring Nicolas Cage, and its follow-up, 2011's Ghost Rider: Spirit of Vengeance.At a separate event at the convention, the actor Ryan Reynolds made a surprise appearance as the Marvel character Deadpool, who he has played in a series of films.This year's convention has ushered in a number of Marvel updates for fans, including an exclusive trailer that was shown of the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday film and an announcement that Black Panther 3 would be released in 2028. Johnny Depp made a special appearance, as did Rick Moranis when he announced a sequel to the 1987 parody film Spaceballs.Before making the big reveal about Gosling's addition to Marvel, Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige said on stage that he had often been asked when Gosling would join the MCU.Shortly after, the lights turned off. When they returned, the actor appeared on stage to cheers from screaming fans.Speaking about the role, Gosling, a three-time Oscar nominee, said: "Wow, is this really happening?"He has previously spoken about his desire to take on the role. Appearing on Josh Horowitz's Happy Sad Confused podcast in March, the Hail Mary and La La Land star confirmed he was in discussions with Marvel.Ghost Rider is the anti-hero identity of motorcycle stuntman Johnny Blaze.The character's story begins when he becomes bound to the Spirit of Vengeance Zarathos after making a deal with villain Mephisto to spare his surrogate father, giving him superpowers.The film will be directed by Shawn Levy, who Gosling described as the "only" director for the project.Levy has previously directed Deadpool & Wolverine in the MCU, and is currently working with Gosling on Star Wars: Starfighter, which is due to be released next year.Levy told the crowd that he and Gosling spent a lot of their downtime on set daydreaming about Ghost Rider and swapping ideas.The director said: "As Ryan started talking about his vision for this character, we started riffing, and I finally said, 'bro, let's ride', so guys, we'll see you in 2028."The other famous Ryan - Reynolds - made his own appearance at a panel for the upcoming Avengers: Doomsday film.

schema.headline: Ryan Gosling to join Marvel Cinematic Universe as Ghost Rider

title: Water returns to Gatwick Airport after major outage
description: Gatwick Airport says its water supply has returned after passengers faced long queues for toilets and closed restaurants and bars after a major supply
body: Gatwick Airport says its water supply has returned after passengers faced long queues for toilets and closed restaurants and bars after a major supply outage.Both terminals at the UK's second busiest airport lost running water on Sunday morning after a power failure at a treatment works that serves the area.People told the BBC of confusion and frustration as all bars and restaurants were shut, some were left with nowhere to sit and waits built up outside toilets.SES Water, the company that supplies the airport, said earlier the power outage was fixed, with Gatwick reporting on Sunday night that water had returned to "the vast majority of the London Gatwick campus".The water company, which also supplies parts of Kent, Surrey and south London, said complications caused by a power outage at Bough Beech treatment works meant some customers had experienced low water pressure or a temporary loss of supply.A spokesperson had earlier confirmed that Gatwick Airport was affected.On Sunday afternoon, SES Water said its treatment works were back up and running, but later added it would take time for the network to fully return to normal as it had been "a highly unusual and complex issue"."We want to reiterate that our teams are working as quickly as they possibly can and we are grateful for everyone's patience," the spokesperson added.Gatwick apologised and said staff had been handing out bottled water.A spokesperson added: "Our staff are on hand to support passengers and provide assistance where needed, some restaurant partners have opened to provide additional seating."Gatwick said additional teams had been deployed across both terminals to support passengers.The airport added there had been no flight cancellations as a result of the supply issues and that it was working closely with SES Water to minimise the impact."Our teams are working hard to reopen toilets and other facilities as quickly and safely as possible," a spokesperson said.BBC reporter Adam Dowling, who was flying from Valencia to Gatwick, said his flight had been delayed because of the water supply disruption and passengers had been informed that landing slots were being moved around "to reduce the number of flights" coming in to Gatwick.The BBC has contacted Gatwick Airport to confirm if there has been any flight disruption.Roger Wood, from Tunbridge Wells in Kent, said he thought his friends were joking when they told him there were no restaurants or bars open in Gatwick's south terminal.When he arrived to meet them ahead of his flight on Sunday, he found "there was no water at all - no Nando's, no Wetherspoon, all of those places were completely shut and stopping people coming in as there was no fresh water or ability to wash hands".Wood told the BBC: "The only place you could buy something was places like Pret and Itsu where it was packaged food, or shops."There was a general grumpiness and the usual frustration at not being able to get a drink at a bar from people, but everybody seemed quite resigned."Wood said people could go in the toilets but there was no way to wash hands and conditions had grown worse in the hour or two they were there.Houchin said there has been "very little information" from the airport."I think people are just fed up because they've got a long wait, but everyone understands there's nothing you can do about it," she added.Ian Bubb, who was flying to Alicante in Spain with British Airways, said there had been a "total lack of information" from the airport."Absolute disgrace at Gatwick - total lack of contingency planning for such an event," he said.The passenger said he had booked a lounge but was not allowed to sit inside.People heading to the airport for flights have been advised not to arrive early.A statement from Easyjet said: "Due to a water supply issue affecting London Gatwick Airport, bag drop desks are temporarily opening two hours before departure instead of three hours."The airline said: "Please do not arrive earlier, as you will not be able to drop off your bags or enter the departure lounge until bag drop opens."SES Water confirmed the Kent postcodes TN8 and TN11 and parts of Surrey postcodes RH1, RH6 and RH10 had no water supply or low pressure. The company said it was delivering bottled water to vulnerable customers.Gatwick Airport and the local area also suffered water issues in July 2022, when low pressure caused by a burst water main affected 1,200 houses and closed toilet facilities at the airport.

schema.headline: Water returns to Gatwick Airport after major outage

title: Tour de France 2026: Tadej Pogacar wins fifth Tour as Mathieu van der Poel takes stage 21
description: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Tadej Pogacar is considered one of the greatest riders of all timeByMatt WarwickBBC Sport Senior JournalistSl
body: Image source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Tadej Pogacar is considered one of the greatest riders of all timeByMatt WarwickBBC Sport Senior JournalistSlovenian Tadej Pogacar won the Tour de France for a record-equalling fifth time.The 27-year-old UAE Team Emirates-XRG rider crossed the line on Paris' Champs-Elysees in the peloton, to join Jacques Anquetil, Eddy Merckx, Bernard Hinault and Miguel Indurain as the endurance event's most successful male riders.All-conquering Pogacar raised the idea that his remarkable reality is proving stranger than fiction, describing it as "something you wouldn't even maybe write in a story book".The three-week Grand Tour's final stage was won by the Netherlands' Mathieu van der Poel of Alpecin-Premier Tech after a frantic charge to the line on the French capital's famous cobbles in which he pipped team-mate Jasper Philipsen of Belgium by inches.Pogacar's victory means he is positioned by many as the greatest cyclist of all time, superseding the achievements and status of Belgian legend Merckx.It also marks Pogacar's third Tour win in succession and includes a record-breaking ascent of the iconic Alpe d'Huez on stage 19, when he sealed another dominant victory.It was the last of five stage wins in a race in which Pogacar used his explosive launch and unmatchable metronomic pace to see off his rivals, who for some time have had virtually no answer.Pogacar has won almost every major race in the sport, including the Tour of Flanders, Giro d'Italia, Milan-San Remo, Road World Championships, Giro di Lombardia and Liege-Bastogne-Liege.Pogacar was booed by some fans during the Tour, as his performances are often so far ahead of any of his peers that some feel frustrated the sport is losing its competitive edge.He now has 127 wins in an eight-year elite professional career."Victory is really special," said Pogacar. "Thank you to all the fans and my team."But the biggest thanks goes to all my family who support me all my life. My parents - without them I would not be standing here five times already."Seven Tours and seven times on the podium, and five wins, is something you wouldn't even maybe write in a story book, and it's unbelievable for me."It's a magnificent podium with some incredible champions to fight with."It's a shame Jonas [Vingegaard] crashed out this time and many others. I hope they have a quick recovery and next year we fight again."High drama on the Champs-ElyseesThe famous final stage, which for the overall contenders is an unchallenged formality, typically becomes a flat bunch sprint.Last year organisers ASO introduced a circuit which takes on a cobbled climb over the city's famous Montmartre hill, changing the parcours enough to encourage the heavier, more powerful riders to challenge for victory.On Sunday it was powerhouse classics legend Van der Poel who took victory after charging away with 11km remaining with Pogacar.Pogacar and Van der Poel led through the picturesque and narrow lanes over Montmartre and past Sacre-Coeur, where some fans had mobile phones knocked out of their hands as the riders squeezed past at speed, before Pogacar began to fade after three weeks of dominance and showing no weakness.Van der Poel, whose strength and staying power allow him to pull out gaps in gruelling one-day races, just managed to stay ahead of a chasing pack which included several sprinters and was rapidly closing, before he crossed the line, collapsed off his bike and lay under a barrier, breathing heavily for several minutes.Van der Poel added this prestigious victory on the famous cobbles to many of the sport's biggest one-day races, such as multiple victories in Paris-Roubaix and the Tour of Flanders.He said: "We have a saying in Dutch that it has to come for your toes. I don't know where this came from, but not from my toes."The stage was reduced from 133km to 89km after the redirection of emergency services to help tackle wildfires in south-west France.Image gallerySkip image galleryImage source, Getty ImagesImage caption, Pogacar leads the peloton past the Arc de TriompheSlide 1 of 5, Tadej Pogacar rides past the Arc de Triomphe, Pogacar leads the peloton past the Arc de TriompheA future beyond Pogacar?The one rider who has broken Pogacar's stranglehold of cycling's biggest race in the past was Denmark's Vingegaard, who won in 2022 and 2023.But this year the 29-year-old Visma-Lease a Bike rider abandoned after breaking his collarbone on a easy right-hand bend on stage 15.The mistake was very unlike Vingegaard's near perfect technique and execution as a rider, and attention soon turned to scrutiny of the International Testing Agency (ITA), which had awoken Vingegaard at 2am to carry out an anti-doping test.Other riders had the same treatment, including Pogacar at 5am, but the ITA said there was "exceptional circumstances" to take the night tests, which are rare and require additional permission.It is not known when the test results will be published.Pogacar's only other real rival was the much-improved Belgian Remco Evenepoel of Red Bull-Bora-Hansgohe, who finished six minutes 26 seconds behind overall.Third place went to Pogacar's Mexican team-mate Isaac del Toro, who won stage two thanks largely to Pogacar's babysitting pace in the lead-up to the line.It would not be the only time Pogacar would aid Del Toro, 22, sacrificing his own potential victory on Saturday's brutal 'queen' stage to Alpe d'Huez to consolidate Del Toro's place on the podium.Del Toro's white jersey for the best young rider came at the expense of France's new 19-year-old star Paul Seixas of Decathlon-CMA CGM. Seixas looked stronger than Del Toro at times on the climbs but faded substantially on Saturday.Many think Seixas will be a rival to Pogacar in the future.Pidcock pleased but Netcompany without a winIn the year when Britain's four-time Tour winner Chris Froome retired, his former team - now known as Netcompany Ineos Cycling - failed to record a stage victory in 21 attempts.Ex-Ineos rider Tom Pidcock of Pinarello-Q36.5 won on Alpe d'Huez four years ago and returned to this race having achieved much with a new team built entirely around him.The 26-year-old did not manage to win a stage, but he and his team will be satisfied with Pidcock's consistent battling riding, which earned him ninth in the general classification to build on third place in last year's Vuelta a Espana.Fellow Briton Adam Yates, 33, showed great tenacity after falling ill on stage 16 and spending two days riding at the back of the field before helping pace Pogacar up a climb for victory on stage 19.Who won which jerseys?One of the most entertaining riders in the race was Ecuador's Richard Carapaz of EF Education-Easypost. He toiled earlier in the race before coming into great form to claim the king of the mountains' polka dot jersey.  He won stage 18 and Saturday's stage 20 after topping the race's highest point first and after 5,450km of climbing.The green points jersey was awarded to Denmark's Mads Pedersen of Lidl-Trek, after tenacious riding on climbs he is not typically strong on to hoover up mid-stage points, alongside winning stage four.He beat a number of sprinters to the jersey, including Philipsen of Alpecin-Premier Tech. Philipsen won stage 17 and fellow Belgian Tim Merlier of Soudal-Quick Step won three bunch sprint stages.Tour de France stage 21 results1. Olav Kooij (Ned/Decathlon-CMA CGM)6. Matej Mohoric (Slo/Bahrain-Victorious)7. Rick Pluimers (Ned/Tudor Pro-cycling)8. Anthony Turgis (Fra/Total Energies)9. Milan Fretin (Bel/Cofidis)10. Remco Evenepoel (Bel/Red Bull-Bora-Hansgrohe) +6mins 26secs3. Isaac del Toro (Mex/UAE Team Emirates-XRG) +9mins 42secs4. Paul Seixas (Fra/Decathlon-CMA CGM) +11mins 56secs5. Lenny Martinez (Fra/Bahrain-Victorious) +13mins 2secs6. Mattias Skjelmose (Den/Lidl-Trek) +14mins 59secs7. Juan Ayuso (Spa/Lidl-Trek) +17mins 48secs8.
